result.document_summary: Official text of California Civil Code § 1950.5, the statewide residential security deposit statute (amended by AB 414, effective Jan. 1, 2026).
result.notes: One security-deposit record for the cap (with the small-landlord two-month exception and the exemption for pre-July 1, 2024 deposits) and one for the return/itemization deadline. Dates in the cap rule follow subdivision (c)(6); the 2026 amendment date is the document's stated effective date for the current text.

rules.title: Security deposit cap
rules.requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive security in excess of one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent. Small natural-person landlords (no more than two rental properties and four units total) may collect up to two months' rent, except from service members.
rules.key_value: one month's rent (two months for qualifying small landlords)
rules.quoted_span: a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month's rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.
rules.coverage_text: All residential rental agreements where the property is used as the tenant's dwelling.
rules.exemptions_text: Does not apply to security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024; advance payment of six months' rent allowed for leases of six months or longer.

rules.title: Security deposit return and itemized statement deadline
rules.requirement: Within 21 calendar days after the tenant vacates, the landlord must furnish an itemized statement of deductions and return the remaining security. Leases may not call any security 'nonrefundable'.
rules.quoted_span: No later than 21 calendar days after the tenant has vacated the premises
rules.coverage_text: All residential rental agreements where the property is used as the tenant's dwelling.
rules.exemptions_text: Itemization documents not required if deductions for repairs and cleaning total $125 or less or if tenant validly waived.
